A Turborepo monorepo keeps shared Prisma models, design tokens, and automated tests aligned so multiple agents can ship features without collisions.

## Novel Pattern Designs
- **Goal:** Keep the hero ritual and community inspiration visible simultaneously without blocking renders.
Community updates stream independently, while ritual updates tap cached personalization payloads.
- **States & transitions:** `idle` → `loading` (skeletons) → `hydrated`.
`PrismCoordinator` enforces transitions and prevents community fetches from blocking ritual rendering.
### Silhouette Overlay & Color Pipeline
- **Flow:** Expo `UploadService` enforces background/contrast rules and writes to Supabase via signed URLs.
UI `SilhouetteRenderer` consumes the derived asset + palette tokens for consistent overlays.
When `processing`, worker job IDs are stored so UI can poll/subscribe; `failed` includes reason codes (contrast, privacy violation, timeout) to inform the user.
## Implementation Patterns
- PascalCase components, kebab-case file names, snake_case DB tables (`garment_items`, `palette_insights`).
- Background jobs retry 5 times with exponential backoff before hitting the DLQ (stored in Postgres for audit).

## Security Architecture
- Postgres `pgcrypto` encrypts sensitive guardian/contact fields.
- Audit logging writes immutable entries for authentication changes, moderation decisions, and data exports.

- Vercel Edge Config caches weather + outfit snippets with ISR; NestJS responses include cache headers so CDN edges honor short TTLs.
- Playwright synthetic monitoring (cron job) hits ritual endpoints to ensure <2s load time on reference devices; telemetry fed into Grafana when breaches occur.
- **Web:** Vercel (Hobby tier).
- **API + workers:** Vercel serverless (Nest adapter) for HTTP; background workers deferred until workload requires dedicated hosts.

TensorFlow.js NSFW model for automated image screening (runs server-side in BullMQ worker); profanity filter using `bad-words` library for text; human moderators review flagged content via Next.js admin console (`apps/web/app/admin/moderation`).
Decision favors control and cost over vendor speed; staffing plan requires 2 moderators during beta (24-hour coverage via rotating shifts).

_Deployment target:_ the community worker ships as its own container (`apps/api/Dockerfile.community-worker`), built from the repository root, running the compiled community bootstrap as an unprivileged user under `tini`, deployed to a free always-on container host: Northflank De

The image installs only the worker's traced dependency tree (`tfjs-core`, `tfjs-converter` and the WASM backend in place of the union `@tensorflow/tfjs`, one NSFWJS model family) and fails its build above 150 MB of `node_modules` (measured size: payload `image`).

_Resource profile:_ one replica at concurrency one, 512 MiB; latency is measured inside the image at 0.2 vCPU and memory as the running container's cgroup `memory.peak` while it screens the largest accepted upload (payload `runtime`).

_Recorded limitations:_ recall against real unsafe imagery is the upstream model's property and is not measured; the term lists have community provenance and no native-speaker review; the safe corpus is stock photography; the beta runs with two moderators.

Policy v2 passes on safe mass (`Neutral + Drawing`, NSFWJS's safe-for-work classes) above a floor chosen on the calibration half only, with every unsafe bound held at its v1 value: Hentai or Porn above 0.35 blocks, Hentai plus Porn below 0.10, `Sexy` below 0.15, and Hentai, Porn
`mobilenet_v2_mid` stays the model: across the three bundled families it withheld least on the calibration half within the memory and dependency budgets (payload `calibration`).

BullMQ's default 5-second idle block and 30-second stalled check cost an idle worker about 4.8 million commands a month, about 9.50 USD, so the community worker blocks for 300 seconds and checks for stalled jobs every 600 seconds.
The database is shared with the API's queues, whose commands are billed on the same database and are outside that measurement.
**ADR-014 Color Analysis Architecture:** Server-side processing (not on-device) for wardrobe color extraction and palette analysis.

**Version:** 1.0

Teen students, commuting professionals, and after-hours social planners get an at-a-glance, hour-by-hour forecast paired with ready-to-wear outfit guidance so every segment of the day feels effortless and confident.

A minimalist, high-luxury interface—akin to browsing a Prada lookbook—paired with crystal-clear weather glyphs and curated wardrobe suggestions that immediately answer “what should I wear?” while celebrating CoutureCast’s weather + fashion + community promise.
**Technical Type:** Hybrid mobile, widget, and wearable experience with community layer
**Complexity:** Level 3 (cross-surface personalization and social moderation)
- Integrations: weather APIs, wardrobe image catalog, personalization rules engine, moderation tooling
### Domain Context
## Success Criteria
- Provide a locale-aware experience from day one: UI copy, weather terminology, and commerce disclosures available in English (US/Canada), Spanish (LatAm), and French (Canada/EU).
- Preserve the couture-level brand experience: every surface (mobile, widget, watch, community) needs the same minimalist, high-fashion polish with zero visual clutter.
- Age 13+ gate with explicit consent flows; parental notice and COPPA safeguards for any future CoutureCast Jr.
- GDPR/CCPA-compliant data handling with transparent TOS, third-party disclosure, and granular opt-in/out controls for personalization and commerce tracking.
- Sponsorship and affiliate links must be clearly disclosed while maintaining brand tone; no dark patterns around conversion prompts.
### Business Metrics

| Daily forecast engagement    | ≥ 1.5 forecast views per user per day                                                                                                 | Validates weather habit formation        |

| Commerce conversion          | ≥ 6% of outfit sessions trigger a brand click-to-buy                                                                                  | Measures sponsorship/affiliate viability |

| D7 / D30 retention           | ≥ 30% / ≥ 18%                                                                                                                         | Tracks cohort health                     |

| “Outfit hit the mark?” score | ≥ 4.6 / 5                                                                                                                             | Measures perceived quality of AI styling |
### MVP - Minimum Viable Product
- AI outfit engine that maps forecast segments (morning commute, midday, evening) to user wardrobe tags
- Lightweight analytics instrumentation covering activation, forecast usage, outfit clicks, and sentiment pulse
### Growth Features (Post-MVP)
- Wardrobe uploads with smart tagging and saved outfit capsules for deeper personalization
### Vision (Future)
- CoutureCast Jr.
- Advanced AI styling: mood-based outfit sets, seasonal drops, and partner co-branded capsules
- **CoutureCast Jr.
- **AR/virtual try-on experiences** – deferred due to high computer-vision investment; revisit once wardrobe capture adoption stabilises.
## Innovation & Novel Patterns
CoutureCast treats functional weather checks as a moment of personal styling—bridging utility and aspiration in one glance.
### Validation Approach
- **Engagement experiments:** A/B tests on locale-based outfit highlight modules and click-to-buy tiles to validate conversion against baseline weather-only experiences.
### Competitive Differentiation
- **AI + closet intelligence:** Outfit recommendations blend localized forecasts with user wardrobe data, leapfrogging weather-only apps.
- **Launch-day localization:** English, Spanish, and French support with regional units keeps CoutureCast relevant in multiple markets immediately.
### Platform Support
- **Desktop/Web:** Responsive web application delivering the same luxury aesthetic, including desktop widget integration for quick-glance weather + outfit cards.
- **Widgets:** Home/lock-screen widgets on mobile mirroring the core forecast + outfit call-to-action.
### Device Capabilities
- Push notifications for weather alerts, outfit reminders, and community engagement pings (opt-in with quiet-hour controls).
- Optional: haptic feedback on wearable notifications to emphasize urgent weather changes (future enhancement).
- Lead with a couture-inspired monochrome palette punctuated by weather-driven accent colors to preserve the “luxury lookbook” sensation.
- Keep motion tasteful and optional—micro-animations (e.g., soft fades on outfit swaps) are sandboxed experiments; static design remains the default until validated.
### Key Interactions
- **Outfit detail view:** full-screen look with garment cards, comfort notes, optional click-to-buy buttons, and save/share actions feeding the community.
- **Wardrobe capture:** guided camera flow for snapping garments, applying tags, and assigning comfort ranges; accessible from profile hub.
## Functional Requirements

**Dependencies:** Enhances FR2 (provides wardrobe data to personalize outfit recommendations)
- Acceptance: Auto-tag suggestion with manual override; completion requires category + comfort rating.
- Acceptance: Saved outfits can be favorited, renamed, and surfaced in recommendations when relevant.
**Dependencies:** Requires FR2 (outfit content to share).

# couture-cast UX Design Specification

CoutureCast delivers a couture-grade daily ritual that fuses precise local weather insights with AI-personalized wardrobe guidance across mobile, widget, and wearable touchpoints so every user starts the day confident and prepared.
track once COPPA workflows are ready.
We will anchor CoutureCast on a hybrid native foundation:
- **Android:** Material 3 (Material You) for adaptive color harmonization, responsive grids, and stateful components.
This keeps development velocity high (ready-made components, accessibility baked in) while giving us room to craft distinctive garment tiles, silhouette modules, and weather-driven motion themes.
Core User Experience
The launch surface compresses CoutureCast’s promise into an instant ritual: local time, real-time weather deltas, and a hero outfit tile appear immediately so users never hunt for context.

Outfit suggestions render as modular tiles on crisp white or transparent backgrounds, making each garment feel merchandised yet shoppable; free-tier mannequins use adjustable black silhouettes (body type + height sliders), and Premium unlocks a silhouette-toggle plus a “My Form”
### 2.2 Novel UX Patterns
Hero copy anchors the signature promise: “It’s the app where the weather instantly becomes a couture outfit that fits my day.”
Free users land in calm couture inspiration—a serene, editorial mood that builds trust through restraint.
### 2.4 Inspiration Benchmarks
- **Clothing Suggestions layout** — Each garment floats on white/transparent tiles, reinforcing our modular outfit card vision and keeping swap gestures intuitive.
- **Outfit builder onboarding** — Lightweight editing controls (background removal, front/back toggle) demonstrate how to expose power features while preserving breathing room.
### 2.5 Core Experience Principles
- **Guidance:** Subtle onboarding tips and microcopy explain silhouette controls and premium themes, then fade so daily use stays clutter-free.
- **Feedback:** Soft haptics, silhouette glows, and gold micro-accents confirm actions; celebrations stay refined unless a major milestone (e.g., premium unlock) warrants a richer motion moment.
**Core palette (all tiers)**
- Primary typography `#111111` (Onyx) for headings and body copy; secondary text `#44444F` for supportive detail.
- Utility grayscale ladder for structure: `#0D0D12` (Black Tie), `#1E1E26` (Graphite), `#3A3A45` (Charcoal), `#5C5C68` (Slate), `#8A8A95` (Fog), `#B8B8C3` (Mist), `#E6E6ED` (Cloud).
- Reserve gold for primary actions, accent dividers, and premium upsell cues to preserve its luxury impact.
- Typography stays pure black/gray; color is never used for copy except for links, which adopt a deep charcoal underline.
**Jewel Radiance** — Emerald `#0D6F62`, Sapphire `#1F4E79`, Wine Red `#722F37`; applied to silhouette overlays, gradients, and premium chart accents.
**Winter Metallic** — Platinum `#C9CDD8`, Steel `#7E889A`, Ice `#E9EDF6`; powers subtle motion backdrops (fog, snow shimmer) and hero card treatments.
Premium themes inherit the monochrome base for typography and structure, layering these palettes through gradients, fabric-inspired motion, and accessory highlights without jeopardizing readability.

- **Hero + outfit names:** Canela (or Playfair Display fallback) at optical sizes 44/52/64 for hero, 28/36 for section titles; weight regular for a couture editorial feel, uppercase tracking +20 for labels.
- **Numerics + data glyphs:** Space Grotesk (or SF Mono fallback) for temperatures, wind speeds, and timestamps to reinforce precision.
- **Accessibility:** Minimum contrast 4.5:1 by keeping text purely black/gray; Dynamic Type and Material’s typography scaling remain enabled.
- **Spacing unit:** 4px base with 8px rhythm for major steps; scale tokens `xxs 4`, `xs 8`, `sm 12`, `md 16`, `lg 24`, `xl 32`, `2xl 48`, `3xl 64`.
Widgets use a 2-column micro grid.
- **Component spacing:** Card padding 24px (free) / 28px (premium), list rows 16px vertical, silhouette controls 20px spacing to keep toggles touch-friendly.
### 3.4 Button hierarchy
Keeps the hero action high contrast without overusing gold.
- **Tertiary/text:** Charcoal link button (`#3A3A45`) with underline on hover; no fill to preserve a lightweight feel for low-risk actions.
**Rationale:** This catalogue maintains the couture monochrome palette, reserves gold for key highlights (logo, hero badge, focus ring), and delivers WCAG-ready contrast for every state.

Component Library
**Hero Ritual Canvas** – composite module containing weather glyphs, time, garment tiles, chip rail, hide/show toggles.
**Modular Outfit Tile** – reusable card for garments with state variations: default, hover, swap preview, locked (premium).

All components inherit spacing tokens (4px base) and color/typography decisions documented earlier so engineering can wire them into a cross-platform design system (e.g., Figma library + code tokens).
- **Hero Ritual Canvas**
- _User actions_: collapse ribbons, swap garments, open planner, post to community.
- _Variants_: split view (desktop), stacked (tablet/mobile), widget hero (2×2 module).
- **Modular Outfit Tile**
- _Actions_: tap to swap, long-press to edit garment, drag into look when building outfits (web/tablet).
- _Variants_: single garment tile, outfit stack tile (multi-layer), widget micro-tile.
- **Chip & Filter System**
- _States_: default, hover/focus (gold ring), selected (filled chip), loading shimmer (data fetching), disabled (filter unavailable).
- _Accessibility_: chips respond to keyboard arrows; aria-pressed communicates selection state.
- _Content_: hero image, weather/location pill, outfit description, engagement counts, CTA cluster (save/import/applaud/flag) plus sponsorship label when applicable.
- _Variants_: square grid card, list row, widget “pulse” card.
- **Planner Day Card**
- _States_: default, AI-suggested (badge + gold glow), edited (pencil icon), conflict (merlot border), synced (check icon), offline (gray overlay).
- _Accessibility_: each slot uses button groups accessible via tab + arrow, success/error announced via polite aria-live.
- _Elements_: banner (success/info/error/loading), toast (success/error/info), inline validation row.
- _Behavior_: banners slide from top with 300 ms animation; toasts auto-dismiss after 6 s unless required.
- **Widget Modules**
- _Weekly planner (4×2)_: four mini-cards with day abbreviation, weather glyph, outfit hint.
- _States_: default, sync-in-progress (fog overlay), warning (merlot border), offline (gray text).
**Native component tailoring**
- Bottom navigation = Material 3 bottom bar with gold active indicator; iOS tab bar uses large titles disabled to keep layout minimal, but focus indicators adopt gold ring.
- Form controls inherit platform behavior yet adopt CoutureCast spacing and label rules (floating labels disabled in favor of stacked labels for consistency across OSs).
UX Pattern Decisions
**Feedback patterns (selected option: Premium accent feedback)**
- **Error/destructive:** Deep merlot (#361F1F background, #B04A4A border) with light text for clear urgency; destructive toasts mirror the same palette to keep mental mapping consistent.
- **Loading:** Slim top progress indicator plus inline banner using fog background and gold shimmer to signal motion without anxiety.
- Inline labels above fields, secondary hint text below in Fog gray, immediate validation with red microcopy.
- Uploaders include thumbnail previews with gold “processing” indicator.
- Medium-width (640px) for settings, full height for closet management; always dim background to 60% opacity and lock scroll.
**Navigation patterns**
- Back navigation defaults to OS gesture plus inline “Back to ritual” link on detail screens.
- White canvas with gold-outline illustration, single sentence of empathetic copy, and a tertiary CTA encouraging action (e.g., “Add your first garment”).
- Use inline banners for low-risk saves; modal confirmations only for destructive actions (delete closet, remove account) pairing merlot CTA with ghost secondary button.
- In-app toasts pinned top-right on desktop, top-center on mobile; push notifications reuse monochrome + gold palette with concise copy.
- Omnisearch field in hero supports garments, looks, and weather—results split into tabs with most relevant surfaced first.
- Relative times (“Updated 2 min ago”) for freshness, absolute timestamps for forecasts/planner entries; calendar picker uses native OS control styled with gold focus rings.
### 8.1 Responsive Strategy
A planner rail can slide in as a third column on ≥1440px layouts when users need the weekly board, otherwise hero + lookbook each own ~45% of the width with generous guttering.
Horizontal outfit shuttles remain scrollable with 64px edge padding so Apple Pencil/Android stylus gestures feel natural.
Community pulse cards follow immediately and bottom navigation highlights the active tab with a gold underline.
**Widgets & wearables (Option 4B + 4C, light skins):** Rich 4×2 widgets expose the weekly planner summary, while compact 2×2 widgets show current look + swap CTA.
All quick surfaces expose success/alert states via the same gold/merlot color cues as the main UI.
- All breakpoints respect 4.5:1 contrast via the monochrome palette; gold is limited to accents with fallback outlines when high-contrast mode is enabled.
- Prefers-reduced-motion suppresses premium motion backdrops in favor of static gradients; watch widgets fall back to solid fills.
**Accessibility commitments:**

- **Keyboard navigation:** Tab order follows hero → chip rail → garment tiles → community cards; provide visible gold focus rings on every interactive element, skip-to-content links on desktop, and trap focus within modals until closed.

- **Testing plan:** Automated audits with Lighthouse + axe DevTools per build, plus manual VoiceOver (iOS) and TalkBack (Android) sweeps for each release candidate; quarterly keyboard-only regression walkthroughs documented in QA notes.

## Versioning model
Breaking changes ship on `/api/v2`; they do not land silently in `/api/v1`.
| CI enforcement         | Optic diffs the canonical spec against `main` and blocks breaking changes unless a major version bump records an explicit versioning decision.
- Patch: descriptions, examples, tags, or other metadata-only changes with no wire-level behavior
- Minor: additive backward-compatible changes such as a new endpoint, a new optional request
- Major: removals, renames, stricter validation, auth requirement changes, enum narrowing, status
If there is doubt, classify the change as breaking.
## Breaking vs non-breaking changes
| Add an optional request field                                            | Non-breaking   |
| Change examples, descriptions, tags, or summaries                        | Non-breaking   |
| Add a required request field                                             | Breaking       |
| Narrow an enum or tighten validation so a previously valid payload fails | Breaking       |

Enables users to photograph or upload clothing items into their private digital wardrobe via camera or file picker with interactive aspect ratio cropping, auto background cleanup matting, real-time byte progress, and guardian consent enforcement.

Consent-Aware Authorization & Guardian Verification: `GuardianService.assertWardrobeUploadAllowed` checks user age and active unrevoked guardian consent directly from Postgres before issuing upload sessions or committing garments for teen accounts (ages 13–15).

Strict OpenAPI & Shared HTTP Contracts: `@couture/api-client/contracts/http` defines strict Zod schemas (`.strict()`) for session allocation, binary relay, and garment commit, rejecting unknown or client-controlled ownership parameters.

Privacy Telemetry & Redaction: `garment_upload_completed` event captures only pseudonymous subject ID, `garment_id`, `file_size_bytes`, `mime_type`, `has_cropping`, `has_bg_cleanup`, and `duration_ms` with PostHog IP capture disabled and Pino logger token redaction.

# Secrets management
## Decision
- Local development uses gitignored `.env` files such as `.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.preview`, and `.env.prod`.
- Hosted environments use provider-native secret stores such as Vercel, Expo EAS, Supabase, Upstash, and other service dashboards.
## Environment workflow
- Keep populated `.env*` files out of version control.
- Prefer `.env.local` for machine-specific overrides.
- Store CI-only values in GitHub Actions repository or environment secrets.
- Rotate tokens when access changes or a leak is suspected.
- Store runtime secrets in the platform that consumes them.
- Keep least-privilege keys for each runtime surface.

# CoutureCast - Product Requirements Document
CoutureCast delivers a daily “style concierge” for everyone 13+ who needs to decide what to wear against real-time conditions.
### What Makes This Special
## Project Classification
**Domain:** Consumer lifestyle (weather × fashion)
- Signals: mobile app + widgets + watch extension, premium wardrobe AI, social community feed
- Outcomes: confidence in outfit planning, elevated brand feel, habitual daily engagement
No special regulatory domain constraints identified; standard consumer privacy and teen-safety considerations apply.

- Deliver an at-a-glance daily planning ritual: users land, see current and hourly outlook, and receive an immediately actionable outfit recommendation that covers school, commute, and evening scenarios.

- Sustain habit-forming engagement by tying weather intelligence to fashion inspiration and community energy—localized outfit highlight prompts, peer feedback loops, and click-to-buy pathways must feel native, not bolted on.

- Localization pipelines must include human review before release with safe fallback to English when translations are missing.

| Metric                       | Target                                                                                                                                | Purpose                                  |

| Activation completion        | ≥ 75% of new users finish profile + first outfit within 2 minutes                                                                     | Confirms onboarding clarity and utility  |

| Outfit detail click-through  | ≥ 35% from “Today’s Look” tiles                                                                                                       | Ensures recommendations feel relevant    |

| Community participation      | ≥ 30% of weekly actives post, react, or comment                                                                                       | Gauges social stickiness                 |

## Product Scope
- Real-time and hourly weather engine with personalized comfort toggles (“I run cold”) and alerting
- Cross-surface delivery: mobile app, home/lock-screen widget, and smartwatch glance with consistent luxury feel
- Multi-locale foundation shipping with English, Spanish, and French translations plus regional units (°F/°C) and legal copy variants
- CoutureCast Community: themed challenges, peer reactions, and curated locale-based outfit highlights
- Premium subscription tier unlocking 7-day lookbooks, advanced AI styling, and ad-free experience
- Commerce flywheel: click-to-buy runway with sponsorships, affiliate links, and curated brand collections

A couture-inspired, minimalist presentation that merges hourly weather intelligence with curated outfit narratives and a social layer.
The triad of weather, fashion, and community in a single mobile-first experience is rare in the category, positioning CoutureCast closer to luxury commerce apps than traditional forecasts.
- **Design validation:** High-fidelity prototype testing with target personas to confirm the “luxury lookbook” sensation while keeping clarity of weather data.
- **Community pilots:** Limited-beta rollouts of the social feed to monitor moderation load, feedback quality, and sentiment before broad release.
- **Multi-surface luxury execution:** Native parity across mobile, widgets, and watch delivers a couture aesthetic competitors lack.
- **Community + commerce loop:** Locale-based highlights, social export, and disclosed affiliate pathways create a monetizable inspiration funnel.
## Platform-Specific Requirements
- **Mobile:** Native support for iOS and Android via React Native, tuned for phones first; tablets inherit responsive layout but receive no bespoke features at launch.
- **Wearables:** watchOS companion glance presenting “Now” outfit summary with swipe-through for the next hourly shift.
- **Localization:** Launch-day support for English (US/Canada), Spanish (LatAm), and French (Canada/EU) with dynamic language switching, locale-aware formatting, and translation QA workflow.
- Cameras & photo libraries for wardrobe item capture and editing.
- Location services (approximate) to auto-detect weather region, with manual override for users who disable GPS.
## User Experience Principles
- Prioritize information hierarchy: current conditions + immediate outfit tile above the fold, hourly ribbon and community hooks directly beneath.
- Maintain accessibility headroom: target WCAG AA contrast and VoiceOver labels in MVP, with a review checkpoint once growth work begins.
- **Hero landing:** stacked layout pairing temperature, condition iconography, and primary “Today’s Look” tile with quick toggles (“Morning commute”, “Evening plans”).
- **Community feed:** vertically scrolling stream of locale-driven challenges and peer posts with lightweight engagement controls (react, comment, report).
- **Widget/watch glance:** distilled “Now” recommendation plus next-hour preview, tapping through to the mobile detail surface.
### FR1 — Weather Intelligence Core _(Phase 1 – MVP)_
The system shall ingest real-time weather data (current + hourly + daily) for a user's active location and refresh at least every 30 minutes.
Users shall be able to pin multiple locations (home, work, travel) and switch between them within two taps.
Weather alerts (temperature swings, precipitation, extreme conditions) shall trigger optional push notifications and appear on the landing card.
### FR2 — Outfit Recommendation Engine _(Phase 1 – MVP)_
The AI engine shall produce at least three scenario-based outfit cards (morning commute, daytime, evening/social) mapped to the hourly forecast.
Users shall calibrate comfort preferences (“I run cold/warm”, material sensitivities) and see outfit adjustments accordingly.
Premium users shall access a 7-day outlook planner with an outfit per day and ability to reshuffle recommendations.
### FR3 — Wardrobe Management _(Phase 3 – Growth)_
Users shall capture garments via camera or photo import, apply categories, materials, and comfort ratings.
Users shall assemble and save custom outfit capsules for reuse.
### FR4 — Community & Social Layer _(Phase 2 – Community Beta)_
FR3 wardrobe-sourced posts are Phase 3; Community Beta ships with direct photo upload.

## Non-Functional Requirements
**Mobile/Web responsiveness:** First contentful paint < 2 seconds on modern 4G connections; widgets refresh within 5 minutes of new weather data.
**Availability:** 99.5% uptime target for core services (weather fetch, outfit engine, sharing workflows) excluding scheduled maintenance.
End-to-end encryption for personal data (wardrobe photos, preferences) in transit; AES-256 at rest in managed storage.
Moderation actions logged with immutable audit trail retained 12 months; escalation workflow protects against staff misuse.
### Scalability
Weather provider rate-limits monitored; implement graceful degradation (cached last-known plus “data delayed” notice).
WCAG 2.2 AA compliance for contrast, focus states, and semantic structure across platforms.
Plan for captioning/transcripts on any video or audio modules introduced post-MVP.
Translation pipeline supporting English, Spanish, and French with fallback strings, release checklists, and human review for marketing-critical copy.
Community moderation supports multilingual content with keyword detection per language and escalation to native-language reviewers within SLA.
Weather API health checks with automatic provider failover and alerting when error rate exceeds 2% in 5-minute window.
Social sharing failsafe: if platform share fails, offer export to camera roll/download with user notification.

## Gap and Risk Analysis
#### Gap-1: Missing Infrastructure Setup Epic
For a greenfield Level 3 project, **Epic 0: Platform Foundation & Infrastructure** is required before Epic 1.
- Stories CC-1.1 through CC-6.5 assume infrastructure exists (Prisma, Supabase, Redis, Socket.io, CI/CD)
- Sequencing will break if attempted as currently documented
- **CC-0.1:** Initialize Turborepo monorepo (create-expo-app, create-next-app, @nestjs/cli per architecture)
- **CC-0.3:** Set up Supabase project (dev/staging/prod) + Storage buckets + RLS scaffolding
- **CC-0.5:** Initialize Socket.io gateway + Expo Push API credentials
- **CC-0.7:** Configure PostHog + OpenTelemetry + Grafana Cloud telemetry stack
- **CC-0.9:** Initialize OpenAPI spec generation + API client SDK tooling
These stories must complete before Epic 1 can begin.
#### Gap-2: Open Technical Questions Unresolved
**Color analysis pipeline:** "Confirm on-device processing constraints, privacy posture, and performance budgets before CC-5.4"
- **Risk:** Privacy implications differ significantly; performance budgets undefined
**Secondary weather provider:** "Evaluate backup API for outage/rate-limit scenarios to satisfy FR1 availability goals"
- **Risk:** Single point of failure for core weather feature; no failover strategy documented
**Moderation tooling stack:** "Select moderation console/vendor integration (in-house vs external) ahead of CC-6.5 to meet 24-hour SLA"
- **Risk:** 24-hour SLA enforceability unknown without tooling selection
**Recommendation:** **RESOLVE BEFORE SPRINT PLANNING**.

The product intentionally balances quick utility with fashion inspiration, moderated community energy, and privacy-first guardrails for teen users while teeing up a future CoutureCast Jr.
### 1.1 Design System Choice
- **iOS:** Apple Human Interface Guidelines (latest 2025 update) for navigation, typography scaling, and motion defaults.
- **CoutureCast Surface Layer:** Shared token set for couture color stories, silhouette treatments, and micro-interactions so both platforms express a single brand voice.
Custom work concentrates on modular outfit tiles, the premium theme orchestrator, and the editorial look-book grid.
### 2.1 Defining Experience
Hourly and weekly strips sit one tap away, and users can hide them to stay in a minimal, “right-now” focus whenever they prefer.
Premium themes layer expressive palettes and motion microstates, while every outfit tile supports one-touch swaps so planning for the day or week stays effortless.

Dynamic look-book shuffling learns from previous outfit approvals to surface smarter alternates; overlay toggles let users glide between minimal and full-detail weather modes; and contextual premium skins introduce subtle aura glows or fabric-inspired textures tied to weather sta
### 2.3 Desired Emotional Response
Premium unlocks tastefully kinetic themes: seasonal palettes and delicate motion backdrops (fog drift, sunrays, soft rain) that mirror live weather while keeping the core ritual composed and focused.

- **WeatherWare (Android)** — Tall hero photography with inline weather stats, left-rail garment toggles, and a bottom 7-day strip show how couture imagery and meteorological data can coexist without clutter.
- **Outfit look-book grid** — Community feed concept mixes “New” and “Following” tabs with soft-shadow cards, mirroring the social inspiration loop we want for trends and nearby looks.
These references inform the CoutureCast signature: hero-led weather visuals, modular outfit tiles, and community grids that feel editorial yet scannable.
- **Speed:** Weather + outfit context loads in under two seconds, with every swap or hide action responding immediately so the ritual never feels laggy.
- **Flexibility:** Users can collapse ribbons, change silhouettes, or shuffle outfits without leaving the hero view—control without UI sprawl.
### 3.1 Color System
- Background `#FFFFFF` and elevated surface `#F5F5F7` keep layouts bright and gallery-clean.
- Signature accent `#C9A14A` gold—applied to the CoutureCast logotype, key CTAs, and appointment moments like the hero outfit card badge.
**Usage guidance**
- Weather icons, data glyphs, card outlines, and controls live within the grayscale ladder for maximum clarity against the white canvas.
**Premium seasonal palettes (upsell unlocks)**
**Autumn Umber** — Maple `#B1683A`, Chestnut `#8C5331`, Wheat `#D9B38C`; introduces warm neutrals, suede textures, and cozy spotlight frames.
**Spring Bloom (future)** — Soft Coral `#F29BA8`, Mist Lilac `#C9B7E5`, Morning Dew `#B8E3D3`; queued for future drops to keep the ritual fresh.
### 3.2 Typography System
- **System text:** SF Pro Text (iOS) / Inter (Android + web) for body copy, captions, and controls; weights 400/500/600 with 1.4 line-height for readability.
- **Type scale tokens:** `display-xxl 64/72`, `display-xl 48/56`, `heading-lg 32/40`, `heading-md 24/32`, `heading-sm 20/28`, `body-lg 18/28`, `body 16/24`, `body-sm 14/20`, `micro 12/16`.
### 3.3 Spacing & Layout
- **Layout grid:** 12-column, 72px max column width, 24px gutters on desktop; collapses to 6-column on tablets, 4-column on mobile.
- **Containers:** Desktop max width 1360px, tablet 960px, mobile edge padding 24px (free) / 20px (widget); hero module spans full width with 80px top/bottom breathing room.
- **Elevation + dividers:** Use 2dp drop on cards, 1px `#E6E6ED` rules, and 8px corner radius to maintain softness.
- **Primary CTA (standard + premium):** Solid `#111111` fill with white label, 999px pill radius, subtle drop shadow, and gold (`#C9A14A`) 2px focus ring.
- **Secondary:** Ghost button with 1px black stroke on transparent fill; hover introduces a `rgba(17,17,17,0.05)` wash so it still feels tactile.
- **Destructive:** Solid merlot (`#B04A4A`) fill with white text and matching hover darken for clarity.

- Tablet: hero sits on top with chips pinned directly beneath, followed by a two-column lookbook grid.
- Mobile: hero, chips, and garment tiles stack vertically; community pulse cards follow immediately with gold-underlined bottom navigation.
- Inline chips manage Personal vs Community vs Sponsored views plus lookbook filters, eliminating page reloads.
- Community cards show success badges, sponsorship labels, and quick actions (save look, import item, applaud) with haptic feedback on mobile.
- Keeps the hero ritual sacred—users always land on weather + outfit context first.
- Scales cleanly across devices while preserving the couture monochrome aesthetic.

### 6.1 Component Strategy
Built as responsive container with tokenized paddings so it can collapse from split view to single column.
Supports silhouette overlay slot + metadata (feels-like temp, fabric notes).
**Lookbook Card** – media-first card with weather/location tags, engagement stats, and CTA cluster (save, import, applaud).
**Planner Day Card** – three-slot layout (morning/midday/evening) with auto-fill badges, manual edit buttons, and calendar sync status pill.
**Widget Modules** – 2×2 quick glance and 4×2 weekly planner, sharing the same typography and icon tokens for platform parity.
**Detailed specifications**
- _Purpose/data_: surfaces time, precise weather deltas, outfit summary, hide/show controls, and entry CTAs (Plan Week, Share Look).
- _States_: default, condensed (when user hides overlays), loading (skeleton for weather + garments), severe-weather alert (merlot top banner), premium theme applied.
- _Accessibility_: focus order hero → chips → garments; announce weather + outfit via aria-live when data refreshes.
- _Purpose/data_: displays garment photo or silhouette overlay, garment name, material tags, temperature suitability icons.
- _States_: default, hover, selected, swap-preview (showing alternate), locked (premium), error (missing image placeholder), disabled (wardrobe syncing).
- _Accessibility_: alt text for garment imagery, 44px minimum size, descriptive aria-label (“Swap pleated maxi skirt”).
- _Purpose_: toggles between Personal/Community/Sponsored views and filters lookbook lists (New, Following, Near me, Brands).
- _Variants_: single-line scrollable row, multi-row filter drawer, icon-leading chip (e.g., location icon for Near me).
- **Lookbook Card**
- _States_: default, hover (raise + show quick actions), saved (gold check), flagged (merlot border), loading skeleton, reported (overlay + moderation status).
- _Accessibility_: card becomes a region with heading (`aria-labelledby`), CTAs reachable via tab order, sponsorship label announced to screen readers.
- _Content_: day label, weather summary, three slots (morning/midday/evening) each with garment chips + notes, AI auto-fill badge, calendar sync status pill.
- _Variants_: vertical stack (mobile), horizontal row (desktop planner rail), widget snippet.
- **Feedback Suite**
- _States_: success (gold gradient), error (merlot), info (fog), loading (fog with gold progress), queued (stacked toasts with max three visible).
- _Accessibility_: role="status" for success/info, role="alert" for errors; ensure focus moves to inline error on validation failure.
- _Quick glance (2×2)_: temperature, look summary, single swap CTA.

- Close via explicit X and swipe-down gesture on mobile; destructive modals require secondary confirm button.

**Desktop / large (Option 1A — split ritual + lookbook):** Hero ritual and community lookbook stay visible side-by-side so users can glance at weather + outfits while browsing social inspiration.

**Tablet (Option 2A — stacked hero, two-column grid):** Portrait stacks the hero module above a two-column lookbook grid; landscape keeps the hero wide with the grid below but pins the chip rail for fast filtering.
